added_failures_note: No suite ran for this figure review and no suite delta is measured; the count is 0 with an empty id list, not the difference of two arms this rubric took.
caption_review: The page figcaption names both panels, the card, the sample basis and the four values, and states what the change was and what it cost; it does not merely repeat the title.

figures_reviewed.kind: two-panel bar chart, booking tangent and whole Newton step, base against collapsed source

rubric.contrast: pass - all text is near-black on white; the base bars are the mid grey #929292 at roughly 3:1 on white, which reads as data without competing with the green arm; the value labels are full contrast.
rubric.data_ink: pass - the four bars are the only data marks; nothing else carries weight.
rubric.decoration: pass - no gridlines, no background fill, no gradient; top and right spines are absent on both panels and only the left scale and bottom category axis are drawn.
rubric.label_collision: pass - no text is clipped at the canvas edge on either panel, the value labels sit clear above their bars, and no label overlaps another or the data; the right panel's 53.76 ms label has clear headroom below the panel title.
rubric.legibility: pass - two side-by-side panels on one 14 in canvas read at a glance: panel titles 'booking tangent' and 'whole Newton step', linear y in ms from zero, paired bars labelled 'base' and 'collapsed', each bar carrying its value above it. The one word a reader cannot resolve without the caption is the arm name 'collapsed' (see finding).
rubric.table_form: pass - four scalars could be tabulated, but the paired bars are the requested before/after form and make the direction and size of the change immediate; the figure is not an error or count table with no visual relationship. It borders on table territory and is accepted because the composer asked for a stage comparison figure and the comparison is clearer as bars.

findings.summary: The rendered PNG's right-hand panel title reads 'whole Newton step', but the only committed revision of this script maps the stage key whole_step to 'whole step' (line 13). The drawing script and the attached artifact therefore disagree, so the picture under review cannot be shown to be the head's own output: either the attachment is a stale render or the delivered markup was drawn from a different revision of the script. The reader sees a legible title either way, so this does not hold the node, but it must be reconciled before the attachment is treated as evidence for the landed figure.

The collapsed arm is drawn in the feature green (#2e8b57) and the base arm in grey (#929292), but the collapsed arm is the regression: 37.86 ms against 27.83 ms on the tangent and 53.76 ms against 42.84 ms on the step. Green conventionally reads as improvement, so a reader who scans by colour rather than by the value labels can read the taller green bar as the better result in a figure whose whole point is that it got worse. A neutral or warning-toned feature colour, or grey for both arms with the change annotated, would remove the inversion.

Each panel sets its own limit from its own maximum (max(values) * 1.25), which gives the left panel a range near 0-47 ms and the right near 0-67 ms. Both start at zero, which limits the damage, but equal bar heights encode different durations across the two panels, so a reader comparing the panels by eye under-reads how much larger the whole step is than the tangent. One y-limit shared by both panels would make the cross-panel comparison honest.

The category labels are the internal arm names 'base' and 'collapsed' (arms = ("base", "collapsed")), and the caption explains the change as selecting one ring set before integrating without ever using the word 'collapsed'. A reader has to infer from position and colour that the green bar is the changed source. Naming the arms in the caption's own terms, or in the axis label, would let the bars be identified from the figure and its caption alone.
